answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake in escrow before it can transact. Like a jetty that only admits boats that have paid harbor dues, entry costs real capital, and the stake is slashed if the identity is caught attesting falsely or running duplicates, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand stakes. A lotus grows one bloom per root, so one stake backs one identity, and trust decays like a willow shedding leaves unless renewed by fresh verified work, so idle sockpuppets fade while honest agents keep standing.
